notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/01 - Foundations - equilibrium, equations of state and the chemical potential/ET-01 - The criterion for phase equilibrium.md
notes.gap: The transfer calculation does not explicitly explain why each transfer is independent or distinguish stationarity from stability.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/01 - Foundations - equilibrium, equations of state and the chemical potential/ET-02 - Equations of state and departure functions.md
notes.gap: The purpose of the Maxwell substitution and the relation of an isothermal derivative to throttling remain compressed.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/01 - Foundations - equilibrium, equations of state and the chemical potential/ET-03 - Partial molar properties.md
notes.gap: The exact Euler reconstruction may look inconsistent with partial molar volumes changing during mixing.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/01 - Foundations - equilibrium, equations of state and the chemical potential/ET-04 - Chemical potential and the Gibbs–Duhem equation.md
notes.gap: The cancellation establishing Gibbs–Duhem and its distinction from opposite absolute deviations need a sharper explanation.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/01 - Foundations - equilibrium, equations of state and the chemical potential/ET-05 - Calculating the chemical potential.md
notes.gap: The real-minus-ideal subtraction and the role of composition held fixed in the EOS integral need linking.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/02 - Fugacity/ET-06 - The Poynting correction (vapour pressure under an inert gas).md
notes.gap: Total liquid pressure and gas partial pressure are distinct, but their contrasting changes in a pressure experiment remain implicit.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/02 - Fugacity/ET-07 - Fugacity, definition and meaning.md
notes.gap: Fugacity as an exponential coordinate can be confused with a rate or with absolute pressure.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/02 - Fugacity/ET-08 - Fugacity from volumetric data and the fugacity coefficient.md
notes.gap: A path integral and an endpoint compressibility can be mistaken for interchangeable measures.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/02 - Fugacity/ET-09 - Worked example, fugacity of steam at 400 °C.md
notes.gap: The numerical example needs an explicit distinction between a smooth supercritical crossover and condensation.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/03 - Activity coefficients and excess Gibbs energy/ET-10 - The activity coefficient and excess Gibbs energy.md
notes.gap: Activity coefficient relative to ideal mixing can be mistaken for escaping tendency relative to the pure liquid.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/03 - Activity coefficients and excess Gibbs energy/ET-11 - Thermodynamic consistency and the one-constant Margules model.md
notes.gap: Why the total excess energy must be differentiated rather than the molar curve alone remains easy to miss.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/03 - Activity coefficients and excess Gibbs energy/ET-12 - Asymmetric models, parameters from data, and multicomponent mixtures.md
notes.gap: The multicomponent derivative minus the mixture excess term is stated without explaining its origin.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/03 - Activity coefficients and excess Gibbs energy/ET-13 - Worked example, liquid oxygen–argon.md
notes.gap: The example compares nonideal vapour enrichment with Raoult but can obscure which phase is oxygen-richer.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/04 - Measuring activity coefficients and freezing-point depression/ET-14 - Measuring activity coefficients.md
notes.gap: The finite-addition example does not explain the opposing requirements of limiting slopes and measurement resolution.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/04 - Measuring activity coefficients and freezing-point depression/ET-15 - Freezing-point depression.md
notes.gap: The nested approximations leading to colligative behaviour need causal ordering.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/04 - Measuring activity coefficients and freezing-point depression/ET-16 - Worked example, ethylene glycol–water freezing and the eutectic.md
notes.gap: Why the higher of two computed freezing temperatures is encountered first, and what remains fixed during freezing, need making explicit.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/05 - Activity-coefficient models/ET-17 - Random-mixing models (Redlich–Kister, van Laar, regular solution theory).md
notes.gap: The perfect-square result and its distinct assumptions versus an empirical polynomial need an explicit algebraic purpose.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/05 - Activity-coefficient models/ET-18 - Flory–Huggins theory for size-asymmetric mixtures.md
notes.gap: Lattice normalisation and the chain-number/segment-number distinction can be confused.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/05 - Activity-coefficient models/ET-19 - Local-composition models (Wilson and NRTL).md
notes.gap: Boltzmann weighting needs a normalisation explanation, and identical dilute fits need distinguishing from identical interior stability.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/05 - Activity-coefficient models/ET-20 - UNIQUAC, UNIFAC and choosing a model.md
notes.gap: Separate excess-energy contributions need linking to how complete activity coefficients combine.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/06 - Phase rule, osmosis, droplets and bubbles/ET-21 - The Gibbs phase rule.md
notes.gap: Counting independent rather than all pairwise equalities and separating amounts from degrees of freedom need sharper teaching.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/06 - Phase rule, osmosis, droplets and bubbles/ET-22 - Osmotic equilibrium.md
notes.gap: The pressure normalisation and composition-dependent endpoint need connecting to reverse osmosis.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/06 - Phase rule, osmosis, droplets and bubbles/ET-23 - Droplets and the Kelvin equation.md
notes.gap: The distinction between Laplace pressure and vapour-pressure enhancement, and the fixed-reservoir stability assumption, need explaining.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/06 - Phase rule, osmosis, droplets and bubbles/ET-24 - Bubbles, superheating and boiling.md
notes.gap: The different compressed phases in bubbles versus droplets and separate meanings of superheat and boiling elevation need connecting.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/07 - Vapour–liquid equilibrium of real mixtures/ET-25 - Binary vapour–liquid equilibrium and its phase diagrams.md
notes.gap: The lever rule derivation and why feed composition belongs to different phases at bubble/dew boundaries need linking.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/07 - Vapour–liquid equilibrium of real mixtures/ET-26 - The γ–φ formulation and Raoult's law.md
notes.gap: Bubble versus dew normalisation and meanings of vapour pure-component versus mixture corrections need clarifying.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/07 - Vapour–liquid equilibrium of real mixtures/ET-27 - Deviations from Raoult's law and azeotropes.md
notes.gap: The two zero-slope factors can obscure why an observable homogeneous azeotrope differs from a spinodal.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/07 - Vapour–liquid equilibrium of real mixtures/ET-28 - Worked example, van Laar parameters from an azeotrope.md
notes.gap: Why the auxiliary ratio simplifies two coupled constants and what the fitted point really constrains need making explicit.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/08 - Solubility of gases in liquids/ET-29 - Gas solubility, the hypothetical liquid and ideal solubility.md
notes.gap: A hypothetical continuation can be mistaken for a physically real supercritical liquid or an arbitrary predicted solubility.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/08 - Solubility of gases in liquids/ET-30 - Worked example, solubility of methane.md
notes.gap: The importance of partial rather than total pressure in comparing gas feeds and solvents remains implicit.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/08 - Solubility of gases in liquids/ET-31 - Henry's law and the Henry standard state.md
notes.gap: Unit dilute-reference activity coefficient may be misread as negligible molecular interactions or high solubility.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/09 - High-pressure vapour–liquid equilibrium/ET-32 - Vapour–liquid equilibrium near critical points.md
notes.gap: The apparent easy flash solution needs an explicit physical experiment distinguishing it from a critical state.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/09 - High-pressure vapour–liquid equilibrium/ET-33 - Retrograde condensation and evaporation.md
notes.gap: Envelope crossings need connecting to conserved overall composition and changing phase compositions; reservoir application needs its limitation.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/10 - Solutes and electrolytes/ET-34 - Dissolved solids and the molality standard state.md
notes.gap: The concentration-scale change needs showing as a logarithmic constant absorbed by the reference.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/10 - Solutes and electrolytes/ET-35 - Ionic solutions, mean activity coefficients and Debye–Hückel theory.md
notes.gap: Why geometric averaging and stoichiometric powers appear is compressed; mean coefficient differs from complete salt activity.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/11 - Liquid–liquid equilibrium and diffusion/ET-36 - Why liquids separate, the curvature of the Gibbs energy of mixing.md
notes.gap: A negative mixing Gibbs energy can be mistaken for proof of homogeneous stability; common tangent is a global comparison.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/11 - Liquid–liquid equilibrium and diffusion/ET-37 - Temperature dependence, consolute points and the vapour–liquid analogy.md
notes.gap: Why heating changes a dimensionless interaction strength even for constant interaction energy needs distinguishing from changing interactions.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/11 - Liquid–liquid equilibrium and diffusion/ET-38 - Worked example, isobutane–furfural liquid–liquid equilibrium.md
notes.gap: Equal activities despite very different concentrations and the separate meaning of lever-rule fractions need interpretation.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/11 - Liquid–liquid equilibrium and diffusion/ET-39 - Binodal, spinodal and the stability of a single liquid.md
notes.gap: Local curvature test needs an explicit finite-versus-infinitesimal fluctuation construction.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/11 - Liquid–liquid equilibrium and diffusion/ET-40 - Diffusion is driven by chemical potential, not concentration.md
notes.gap: Flux factorisation needs separating molecular mobility from thermodynamic restoring force and explaining a negative effective coefficient.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/11 - Liquid–liquid equilibrium and diffusion/ET-41 - Example, diffusion near the nitrobenzene–hexane consolute point.md
notes.gap: Raising a factor below one to an exponent below one can be misinterpreted as speeding diffusion generally or preventing critical slowdown.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/12 - Vapour–liquid–liquid equilibrium and steam distillation/ET-42 - Vapour–liquid–liquid equilibrium.md
notes.gap: Fixed three-phase temperature can seem incompatible with changing composition and phase amounts during boiling.

notes.path: other/obsidian/CEBT-II Notes/Equilibrium Thermodynamics/12 - Vapour–liquid–liquid equilibrium and steam distillation/ET-43 - Steam distillation.md
notes.gap: Pure vapour pressures can be confused with equal dilution or with liquid-layer amounts; equilibrium steam ratio versus operating consumption needs interpretation.
